parsed.explanation: The combined regime has tier-1 state-imposed exposures: entry and visa rules require birth-sex markers and treat sex doubt as refusal or fraud; federal and division rules bar congruent facilities, with the division school rule binding visitors and no local service remedy. Outed travelers can face confiscation/stranding, permanent inadmissibility if misrepresentation, arrest/removal, and if detained national custody conversion and immigration abuse. Courts block or litigate some orders, but the passport rule was upheld, the division repealed protection, and no operative traveler remedy is shown. Severity dominates: no execution or routine detention, but consequences are severe, universal, and partly unremedied.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas use birth-sex; X stopped; existing X until expiry. Visa officers must doubt/refuse mismatched records; suspected material misrepresentation can create permanent lifetime ineligibility. Travelers report confiscation/blocking and stranding; foreign advisories signal border friction.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation, legal-aid FAQ, some existing passports remain valid; court challenge to passport policy unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: A document mismatch can become visa refusal and, if fraud alleged, inadmissibility; division cannot provide remedy where service denied.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections adopted conversion-style treatment (hair cut, hormone removal, psych therapy/drugs); reporting stopped. Immigration custody: forced labor, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse. Arrested trespassers may be held in birth-sex ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented as operative; court cases/injunctions exist but no traveler custody remedy shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility arrest or custody encounter can trigger birth-sex placement, medication denial, abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars congruent government-funded single-sex facilities; many state/provinces ban public buildings, some private; four criminalize in some cases. Division school rule binds all visitors on grounds to birth-certificate restrooms; no adult single-person alternative.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Other state/provinces/local ordinances? Not documented in division; national protections may remain but not reliable.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National funding/school policies reinforce state bans; school visits expose adult visitors; trespass arrest can follow refusal.

care_services.exposure: Adult traveler care denial not documented, but custody removes hormone meds and denies care; division bans gender-affirming care under 18 and limits school topics; public insurance proposal bars youth care.
care_services.protection: Not documented; some litigation may preserve adult coverage elsewhere, not visitor.
care_services.interaction: Minor travelers with gender-affirming needs face denial; adult care continuity uncertain if outed at facilities/emergency.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names radically pro-transgender as violent group trait; law-enforcement directed at schools/teachers facilitating social transition; division stripped civil-rights remedy; public opinion supports birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo does not make trans status reward criterion; national hate-crime statute remains; some courts restrain orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing may increase discretionary harassment/removal but no documented routine trans sweeps or entrapment.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor visitor at school grounds covered by birth-certificate facilities; student single-person alternative needs guardian consent. Adult guardian may face refusal/removal at school/public facility; care and social transition risks if trans minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family trips into schools/campuses become document/facility checks; guardians could be confronted.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific trans killings or assault counts; monitoring says undercounts. Public opinion restrictive; state/province legal risk worst. Police can arrest facility trespass and may apply biased removal.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; some state/local protections elsewhere, not division; no documented protective police record.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street risk unclear; legal hostility and police facility enforcement may escalate encounters.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division removed service/housing remedy; national suit pending; several orders blocked but enforcement varies; traveler cannot rely on domestic self-ID or resident protections.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Court challenges, legal-aid FAQ, possible consular travel advisories from foreign governments; no operative local traveler remedy documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Document mismatch may become immigration case; facility dispute may become criminal trespass; judicial relief uncertain during travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: that regime bars entry with humiliation but no custody; this adds school/public facility exclusion, trespass arrest risk, birth-sex custody, medication removal, and immigration abuse.

Above 0.25-C: no standalone cross-dressing statute or routine detention; facility arrest requires refusal and entry is mostly refusal/stranding. Still close because custody and school rules are severe.
Lower than 0.45-D: registration/database exposure there yields delay/harassment with uncommon charges and no credible prison; here facility/custody exposure and visa fraud bar are more consequential.

parsed.synthesis: National document and facility rules create routine outing at borders, checkpoints, and any government or school setting. The division removes local recourse, so refusal/arrest can be handled by federal or state authority. If encounter becomes immigration or corrections custody, birth-sex placement, medication removal, and abuse follow. Court litigation and partial orders may reduce certainty but do not give traveler-facing protection. The result is a high-severity, universal exposure short of routine detention/execution.
